transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that brought you in today?

Well… I suppose it’s a little embarrassing, but it’s mostly driving over those long bridges toward Miami. The moment my car gets onto one, my chest tightens and my hands just clamp down on the wheel. I suddenly feel like I have to get off right away, even though of course there’s nowhere to go. It’s probably silly, but it’s started to trouble me enough that I thought I should ask someone.
Does this feeling of anxiety happen only when you're driving over long bridges, or have you experienced it in other situations as well?

It’s mostly that, doctor—the long bridges over open water. I mean, I know perfectly well those bridges have been there for years, and people cross them every day without making a fuss. But when I think about being out there over all that water, the fear just feels… much bigger than the actual danger, if that makes sense.
Have you ever experienced similar feelings of anxiety in other situations, like in crowds, public places, or when separated from home?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I don’t especially love crowded places at my age, but I wouldn’t say it’s the same kind of feeling. And being away from home hasn’t bothered me in that way. It’s really more that bridge situation… if that’s the sort of distinction you mean, doctor.
